neighbours.label: connective tokens (without, versus, or, are) inside a description of how shapes or regions are arranged in space: overlapping, tiling, gaps, intersecting
fire: Square tiles can cover a bathroom wall completely without gaps between them.
In the layout editor you can pick stacked panels versus side-by-side panels.
The routine tests whether two polygons are touching or one contains the other.
Bricks in a running bond fill the wall without any holes or overlaps.
The algorithm decides if the two boxes are overlapping or merely adjacent.
Packing circles into a square always leaves gaps, unlike packing hexagons without spaces.
Designers often compare floating windows versus tiled windows on large monitors.
The game asks whether the shaded regions are disjoint or partly overlapping.
quiet: She finished the long exam without any help from her friends.
In the election you can pick the mayor versus the governor as the main race.
The teacher asked whether the two essays are finished or still drafts.
He crossed the whole desert without any food or water.
The manager decides if the two clerks are working or merely chatting.
Running a marathon always leaves you tired, unlike walking a mile without effort.
Critics often compare old films versus new films at the festival.
The quiz asks whether the old stories are true or partly invented.
